executiveSummary: The forecast missed by 14,021 contacts, an 85.4% under-forecast, because the plan was set too low and did not adjust to rising demand.
The plan entered the week 34% below the typical level for this time of year and failed to respond to available signals that demand was increasing.
Evidence supports this conclusion with High confidence (76%), though multiple explanations fit the data and the plan was revisited without correction.
narrative.rootCauseStatement: The plan was set at 16,423 contacts for a week that has averaged 25,062 across two prior years -- 34% below what this week of the year normally brings -- and demand of 30,444 was in line with the week's own history, so the plan is the outlier, not the demand.
narrative.confidenceExplanation: Confidence is High at 76%. recommendationNarratives.text: Review the seasonal baseline and re-levelling logic for this queue: the plan entered the period away from the level this week of the year reliably brings.

Incorporate the identified leading signal and its observed lag into the forecast process (signal: demand_momentum, same_week_seasonal_pattern, holiday_transition): the signal was available before the week and the plan did not respond adequately to it.
Review the re-forecast method itself, not the cadence: the plan WAS reissued during this miss run and the revised plan kept missing the same way.

4_business_impact.statement: 14,021 contacts more than planned in FY26 FW37.

supporting.text: The plan was set at 16,423 contacts for a week that has averaged 25,062 across 2 earlier years (FW202437 28,602, FW202537 21,523) -- 34% below what this week of the year normally brings, and 19% below the queue's usual 20,176. Demand of 30,444 is in line with the week's own history, so the plan is the outlier, not the demand.
supporting.source: Plan vs seasonal norm (same week, prior years)

supporting.text: Against an expected 25062.5 contacts (median demand in fiscal week 37 across 2 prior year(s)), the plan sat 8639.6 contacts below expectation and demand landed 5381.5 contacts above it.
Forecast response: wrong direction. The expected level implied moving the forecast 8262.59 contacts, but it moved -377.01 -- the opposite way.
Units actually in the market under warranty moves with demand in the same week, with enough history behind it to use.

Holiday calendar: Columbus Day. Columbus Day falls in this week. Weeks containing a holiday have historically run 5.57% below this queue's non-holiday level, across 27 week(s), moving that way in 63.0% of them -- not consistent enough to rely on. The plan for those weeks moved -5.27%, so the pattern was reflected in the forecast historically. Forecast capture: inconsistent history -- This queue's response to holiday weeks has not been consistent (63.0% moved the same way), so the forecast cannot be held to it.

The population was close to plan, but contacts per unit differed: 0.0016 actual against 0.0010 planned. The two effects sum to the whole +14,021-contact gap (+2,995 from population, +11,026 from contact rate), so nothing is left unexplained by the split.

The plan WAS reissued 1 time(s) during the 5-week under-forecast run -- at FW202636 (plan set to 16,800) -- and every one of the 2 week(s) since the last reissue has still missed in the same direction. This is not a plan nobody revisited; it is a plan that was revisited and stayed wrong.

contradictory.text: 2 driver(s) track demand when you compare totals across the whole period, but not from one week to the next — actual units under warranty (Actual_ASU) scores +0.47 across the period but only +0.02 week to week; planned units under warranty (Planned_ASU) scores +0.50 across the period but only -0.00 week to week. Two figures that both drift the same way over years without moving together in any given week are following a shared trend, not driving each other, so none of them can carry a cause here. (This is about raw totals versus week-to-week change — nothing to do with Region or Country level.)
1 driver(s) do not track this queue's demand at all — planned units for delivery (shipment) (Final_Units) r=+0.13 — so a driver-based explanation is not available for this queue.
This queue's response to holiday weeks has not been consistent (63.0% moved the same way), so the forecast cannot be held to it.
The measures do not agree, so no single statistical story is settled.
Weekend impact cannot be isolated from fiscal-week totals because day-level actual and forecast data is unavailable in the source.
8 other hypothesis(es) survived and explain the same movement, so this one is not uniquely supported.

7_recommendations.impact: Distinguishes a process that was not run from a process that was run and produced the same error -- they need different fixes.

11_criticality.statement: Critical: 14,021 contacts against plan, about 71% of a typical week for this queue. Already at the highest band, so the lift did not change it, but note that the gap is 71% of a typical week for this queue (19,750 contacts), at or above the 50% lift threshold.
11_criticality.basis: The absolute gap of 14,021 contacts sets the band; the relative gap and persistence may lift it by at most one step and can never lower it.
11_criticality.how_to_read: Criticality is how much this miss MATTERS operationally. It is calculated from the size of the gap in contacts, that gap against a typical week for this queue, and whether the miss is standing or isolated. It is NOT derived from confidence, and a high confidence score can sit beside a low criticality band without contradiction.
11_criticality.not_confidence: Confidence says how strong the evidence is. Criticality says how much the miss matters. They are independent by design.

executiveSummary: The forecast for Social Media China Basic in FY27 FW03 over-estimated demand by 29.5%, or 761 contacts.
This miss is part of a persistent pattern: the plan has been too high in the same direction for 13 weeks, averaging 1,131 excess contacts per week.
The evidence does not allow a definitive cause to be named; confidence in the assessment is Low due to contradictory signals in the data.
narrative.rootCauseStatement: Over-forecast of 29.5% — 761 contacts against plan, and this is not a one-off: the plan has been out in the same direction repeatedly, averaging 1,131 contacts a week over 13 weeks.

limitations: Business Event Repository is not deployed, so this is NotApplicable and carries no confidence penalty (BR-202).

executiveSummary: The forecast for Social Media China Basic in FW202601 was an over-forecast of 7,443 contacts, or 63.8% adherence.
The miss happened because the plan did not properly account for the Spring Festival Golden Week holiday, which historically reduces demand by about one-third, and instead over-reacted to it.

Confidence in this explanation is Medium (66%) because while multiple lines of evidence point to the holiday effect, there are also contradictory signals and the statistical measures do not fully agree.
narrative.rootCauseStatement: The forecast error is drifting, not just noisy: adherence has moved about +1.48 points per week, roughly +19 points across 13 weeks, steadily further into over-forecast. The baseline is decaying and will keep missing in this direction until it is rebuilt.
narrative.confidenceExplanation: Confidence is Medium (66%). The score reflects a balance of strengths and weaknesses: data are fully available, context is complete, and evidence comes from multiple sources, but statistical agreement is weak (less than half of the metrics support the conclusion), model agreement is split, and there is a notable amount of contradictory evidence that reduces certainty.
limitations: Business Event Repository is not deployed, so this is NotApplicable and carries no confidence penalty (BR-202).
The measures do not agree, so no single statistical story is settled.
The same fiscal period in prior years does not show this movement, so a seasonal reading is not supported.
Weekend impact cannot be isolated from fiscal-week totals because day-level actual and forecast data is unavailable in the source.
8 other hypothesis(es) survived and explain the same movement, so this one is not uniquely supported.
The drivers that look related to demand only track it across the period as a whole, not week to week, so the direction of cause cannot be established from this data.
Final_upp_units was required by BUS-02 but has no usable history for this queue, so that relationship could not be tested either way.

1_executive_summary: The forecast for Social Media China Basic in FW202601 was an over-forecast of 7,443 contacts, or 63.8% adherence.
The miss happened because the plan did not properly account for the Spring Festival Golden Week holiday, which historically reduces demand by about one-third, and instead over-reacted to it.

executiveSummary: The forecast for Social Media China Premium in FW202602 over-estimated demand by 7,529 contacts, or 39.7% of plan.
The miss happened because the forecast over-reacted to leading signals that were present before the week, and demand moved away from what those signals suggested.
We are highly confident in this explanation, with no adjustments needed to the confidence score.
narrative.rootCauseStatement: The forecast error is drifting, not just noisy: adherence has moved about +0.32 points per week, roughly +4 points across 13 weeks, steadily further into over-forecast. The baseline is decaying and will keep missing in this direction until it is rebuilt.

The score reflects strong statistical agreement, complete context, and solid evidence strength, tempered by moderate contradictory evidence and historical consistency.

recommendationNarratives.text: Incorporate the identified leading signal and its observed lag into the forecast process (signal: demand_momentum, holiday_transition, driver_movement:Final_Units): the signal was available before the week and the plan did not respond adequately to it. This turns a signal the process already receives into a plan movement, which is where this miss was avoidable.

Review the re-forecast method itself, not the cadence: the plan WAS reissued during this miss run and the revised plan kept missing the same way. This distinguishes a process that was not run from a process that was run and produced the same error -- they need different fixes.
Re-base this queue's forward plan to its current run rate. This removes a standing gap that repeats every week until corrected.

4_business_impact.statement: 7,529 contacts fewer than planned in FY26 FW02.

supporting.text: The forecast error is drifting, not just noisy: adherence has moved about +0.32 points per week, roughly +4 points across 13 weeks, steadily further into over-forecast. The baseline is decaying and will keep missing in this direction until it is rebuilt.
Against an expected 16012.0 contacts (median demand in fiscal week 2 across 2 prior year(s)), the plan sat 2976.16 contacts above expectation and demand landed 4553.0 contacts below it.
Forecast response: over response. The forecast moved 8896.13 contacts against the 5919.97 implied -- it over-reacted.
Units actually in the market under warranty moves with demand in the same week, with enough history behind it to use.
Planned units for delivery / production (shipment) moves with demand in the same week, with enough history behind it to use.

Holiday calendar: Spring Festival Golden Week holiday. Spring Festival Golden Week holiday fell shortly before this week, so this week is the wind-down. The source row flags no holiday for this week, which is correct -- the effect reaches in from an adjacent week. Weeks following a holiday have historically run 4.22% below this queue's non-holiday level, across 12 week(s), moving that way in 58.3% of them -- not consistent enough to rely on. The plan for those weeks moved -2.52%, so the pattern was reflected in the forecast historically. Forecast capture: inconsistent history -- This queue's response to post holiday weeks has not been consistent (58.3% moved the same way), so the forecast cannot be held to it.

Both mattered: the population differed from plan AND contacts per unit differed. The two effects sum to the whole -7,529-contact gap (+14,136 from population, -21,665 from contact rate), so nothing is left unexplained by the split.

The plan WAS reissued 4 time(s) during the 19-week over-forecast run -- at FW202536 (plan set to 15,612), FW202540 (plan set to 18,478), FW202546 (plan set to 18,684), FW202601 (plan set to 10,092) -- and every one of the 2 week(s) since the last reissue has still missed in the same direction. This is not a plan nobody revisited; it is a plan that was revisited and stayed wrong.

contradictory.text: 3 driver(s) track demand when you compare totals across the whole period, but not from one week to the next — actual units under warranty (Actual_ASU) scores +0.84 across the period but only +0.06 week to week; planned units for delivery (shipment) (Final_Units) scores +0.38 across the period but only +0.18 week to week; planned units under warranty (Planned_ASU) scores +0.83 across the period but only +0.08 week to week. Two figures that both drift the same way over years without moving together in any given week are following a shared trend, not driving each other, so none of them can carry a cause here. (This is about raw totals versus week-to-week change — nothing to do with Region or Country level.)
This queue's response to post holiday weeks has not been consistent (58.3% moved the same way), so the forecast cannot be held to it.

executiveSummary: The forecast missed by 4,651 contacts, coming in 36% below plan for Social Media English Basic in the United States during FW202715.
The miss happened because the plan was set too low for this time of year and then moved in the wrong direction when a clear seasonal signal was present.
We are highly confident in this explanation, though the evidence does not point to a single, unique cause.
narrative.rootCauseStatement: The plan was set at 12,793 contacts for a week that has averaged 18,795 across 3 earlier years (FW202415 20,423, FW202515 19,362, FW202615 16,601) -- 32% below what this week of the year normally brings, and 34% below the queue's usual 19,502. Demand of 17,444 is in line with the week's own history, so the plan is the outlier, not the demand.
narrative.confidenceExplanation: Confidence is High (71%). No confidence cap was applied because all evaluated gates were passed: data was fully available, no business rule contradicted the conclusion, period coverage was complete, the primary driver was present, contradictory evidence remained above the threshold, evidence came from multiple sources, the conclusion survived cross-examination, and the volume band was not emerging.
limitations: Business Event Repository is not deployed, so this is NotApplicable and carries no confidence penalty (BR-202).

recommendationNarratives.text: Review the seasonal baseline and re-levelling logic for this queue: the plan entered the period away from the level this week of the year reliably brings. This follows the FORECAST_BASELINE_FAILURE mechanism.

Incorporate the identified leading signal and its observed lag into the forecast process (signal: same_week_seasonal_pattern): the signal was available before the week and the plan did not respond adequately to it. This follows the FORECAST_RESPONSE_FAILURE mechanism.
Re-base this queue's forward plan to its current run rate.

executiveSummary: The forecast for Social Media English Basic in FY26 FW43 missed by 50%, or 7,173 contacts, with actual demand coming in above plan.
The miss happened because the forecast did not adjust to available signals and the baseline was too low, and these two issues together drove the error.
We have medium confidence in this explanation because the evidence is mixed, with some measures agreeing and others not, and no single statistical story is settled.
narrative.rootCauseStatement: The forecast error is drifting, not just noisy: adherence has moved about -2.60 points per week, roughly -34 points across 13 weeks, steadily further into under-forecast. The baseline is decaying and will keep missing in this direction until it is rebuilt.
narrative.confidenceExplanation: Confidence is Medium (63%). The score reflects a balance of strengths and weaknesses: data are fully available, context is mostly complete, and evidence strength is solid, but statistical agreement is low, model agreement is split, contradictory evidence nearly balances the support, and historical consistency is only moderate. No confidence cap was applied because all gates were passed.
limitations: Business Event Repository is not deployed, so this is NotApplicable and carries no confidence penalty (BR-202).
The measures do not agree, so no single statistical story is settled.
The same fiscal period in prior years does not show this movement, so a seasonal reading is not supported.
No established direction exists for this queue, so the movement cannot be attributed to a continuing trend.
No driver relationship reached the strength and stability required to be used, so any lag would be assumed rather than measured.
Weekend impact cannot be isolated from fiscal-week totals because day-level actual and forecast data is unavailable in the source.
6 other hypothesis(es) survived and explain the same movement, so this one is not uniquely supported.
The drivers that look related to demand only track it across the period as a whole, not week to week, so the direction of cause cannot be established from this data.
Final_upp_units was required by BUS-02 but has no usable history for this queue, so that relationship could not be tested either way.
This queue's response to holiday weeks has not been consistent (62.1% moved the same way), so the forecast cannot be held to it.

recommendationNarratives.text: Review the seasonal baseline and re-levelling logic for this queue: the plan entered the period away from the level this week of the year reliably brings. This corrects a standing level error that repeats every week until the baseline is reset and follows the FORECAST_BASELINE_FAILURE mechanism.

Incorporate the identified leading signal and its observed lag into the forecast process (signal: demand_momentum, holiday_transition): the signal was available before the week and the plan did not respond adequately to it. This turns a signal the process already receives into a plan movement, which is where this miss was avoidable and follows the FORECAST_RESPONSE_FAILURE mechanism.

Review the re-forecast method itself, not the cadence: the plan WAS reissued during this miss run and the revised plan kept missing the same way. This distinguishes a process that was not run from a process that was run and produced the same error -- they need different fixes and follows the plan_revised_but_remained_wrong mechanism.

4_business_impact.statement: 7,173 contacts more than planned in FY26 FW43.

supporting.text: The forecast error is drifting, not just noisy: adherence has moved about -2.60 points per week, roughly -34 points across 13 weeks, steadily further into under-forecast. The baseline is decaying and will keep missing in this direction until it is rebuilt.
Against an expected 18106.0 contacts (median demand in fiscal week 43 across 2 prior year(s)), the plan sat 3765.85 contacts below expectation and demand landed 3407.0 contacts above it.
Forecast response: wrong direction. The expected level implied moving the forecast 2908.09 contacts, but it moved -857.76 -- the opposite way.

Holiday calendar: Thanksgiving Day. Thanksgiving Day falls in this week. Weeks containing a holiday have historically run 4.0% below this queue's non-holiday level, across 29 week(s), moving that way in 62.1% of them -- not consistent enough to rely on. The plan for those weeks moved -5.46%, so the pattern was reflected in the forecast historically. Forecast capture: inconsistent history -- This queue's response to holiday weeks has not been consistent (62.1% moved the same way), so the forecast cannot be held to it.

Both mattered: the population differed from plan AND contacts per unit differed. The two effects sum to the whole +7,173-contact gap (+2,844 from population, +4,329 from contact rate), so nothing is left unexplained by the split.

The plan WAS reissued 2 time(s) during the 11-week under-forecast run -- at FW202636 (plan set to 16,800), FW202640 (plan set to 16,097) -- and every one of the 4 week(s) since the last reissue has still missed in the same direction. This is not a plan nobody revisited; it is a plan that was revisited and stayed wrong.

contradictory.text: 2 driver(s) track demand when you compare totals across the whole period, but not from one week to the next — actual units under warranty (Actual_ASU) scores +0.46 across the period but only -0.04 week to week; planned units under warranty (Planned_ASU) scores +0.49 across the period but only +0.00 week to week. Two figures that both drift the same way over years without moving together in any given week are following a shared trend, not driving each other, so none of them can carry a cause here. (This is about raw totals versus week-to-week change — nothing to do with Region or Country level.)

Treat as weak supporting evidence and do not make it a primary cause.

executiveSummary: The forecast for Social Media China Premium in FY26 FW35 was set at 2,163 contacts but actual demand was 9,115 contacts, a miss of 6,952 contacts.
The miss occurred because the plan entered the week at the wrong level and failed to respond appropriately to a repeatable seasonal and holiday signal that was visible in advance.
Confidence in this assessment is High, based on strong evidence across multiple dimensions, though the statistical story is not fully settled and other hypotheses remain viable.

This distinguishes a process that was not run from a process that was run and produced the same error -- they need different fixes. This follows the plan_revised_but_remained_wrong mechanism.

1_executive_summary: The forecast for Social Media China Premium in FY26 FW35 was set at 2,163 contacts but actual demand was 9,115 contacts, a miss of 6,952 contacts.
The miss occurred because the plan entered the week at the wrong level and failed to respond appropriately to a repeatable seasonal and holiday signal that was visible in advance.
Confidence in this assessment is High, based on strong evidence across multiple dimensions, though the statistical story is not fully settled and other hypotheses remain viable.
